title: M:N Free Sewing
content: **List of Contents** M: N Free Sewing Create M: N Free Sewing Delete vs Esc Unlink M: N Sewing **M: N Free Sewing** \- Freely create Sewing Lines to sew multiple Patterns to multiple Patterns at once. \- Hold down the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115022568807/mceclip0.png) **Free Sewing** tool to access the child menu. Click the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115022568847/mceclip1.png) **M: N Free Sewing** tool. \- Or, navigate to the Main Menu and select Sewing ▶ **M: N Free Sewing.** ** ****Create M: N Free Sewing** \- When the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115022568847/mceclip1.png) **M: N Free Sewing** tool is selected, a comment will appear next to the mouse cursor guiding to begin creating M Sewing Lines. \- Establish the start and end points on the Pattern outlines that belong to M Sewing Lines. To complete the M Sewing Lines, hit the Enter key on the keyboard. \- A comment will appear next to the mouse cursor guiding to begin creating N Sewing Lines. \- Repeat the same process as creating the M Sewing Lines. \- Hit the Enter key on the keyboard to complete M: N free Sewing Lines. **Delete vs Esc** \- Delete: hit the Delete key on the keyboard to cancel the latest action. \- Esc: hit the Esc key on the keyboard to cancel the entire action. **Unlink M: N Sewing** \- Select the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115022634928/mceclip2.png) Edit Sewing tool from the 2D toolbar. \- Right-click on the Sewing Line and select Unlink M: N Sewing from the pop-up menu. \- The selected M: N Sewing Lines will be unlinked and they can be edited individually. Go back to the List of Contents
content_description: This web page provides a comprehensive guide on utilizing the M: N Free Sewing tool in Clo3D for creating and managing multiple sewing lines across patterns efficiently.

title: I forgot my license ID and password. (CLO below 2024.0)
content: * Please note that the below guideline applies to users who are using CLO version below 2024.0. If you are using CLO 2024.0 and above, please sign in with CLO-SET. **Question** I'm using CLO version below 2024.0 and I forgot my license ID and password. What should I do? **Answer** **Find license ID** To find your license ID, please follow the indicated guideline below: 1. Go to CLO website and click on '[Sign in](https://clo3d.com/en/signin)'. 2. If you forgot your ID but remember the email address used for sign-up, please use the email address to sign in. 3. You can find your ID on the [Account page](https://www.clo3d.com/accounts). However, if you forgot both the license ID and the email address used for signing in, please reach out to CLO via [Contact Us](https://www.clo3d.com/support/contactus) page. **Find Password** Please refer to the following article to reset your license password. * [How can I reset my password on CLO Web and the Software?](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/29936192175129-How-can-I-reset-my-password-on-CLO-Web-and-the-Software)
content_description: This web page provides guidance for users of CLO versions below 2024.0 on how to recover their license ID and password.

title: Fold/Sew Pleats
content: **Objective** Create a variety of pleats, fold and sew them (ver2.3.0). ** Location** Main Menu ▶ 2D Pattern ▶ Pleats ▶ **Pleats Fold** / **Pleats Sewing** 2D Toolbar ▶ ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/article_attachments/115001057348/________.png)**Pleats Fold** / ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/article_attachments/115001012867/________.png)**Pleats Sewing** ** Operation** **Pleats Fold** 1. Select the tool/menu indicated in Location. 2. Click to establish the initial point for the direction of the pleats, then double-click to establish the end point. → Pleats Fold window appears. 3. Select a desired type of pleats. → Depending on the selected pleats type, the Fold Angles of the Internal Lines are now being highlighted. **※****Note:** Yellow: Outside fold line (Fold angle of zero(0) degree), Light-blue: Inside fold line (Fold angle of 360 degree), Not highlighted: No fold line (Fold angle of 180 degree) 4. Check the **Reverse Direction** option as needed. **→** The direction of pleats being folded are now being reversed. 5. Click **OK** button to complete. **Pleats Sewing** 1. Select the tool/menu indicated in Location. 2. Click on the initial point and drag up to the end point of the seamline on the pleats Pattern. ※**Note:** In case of sewing the pleat pattern only, press enter to proceed to the next step. (ver 6.0) 3. On the pleats Pattern, click on the first Sewing Line to begin with, and move the mouse to the end point. → Sewing is now being established for every three(3) segments (the amount of segments needed to create each individual pleat). 4. Click on the end point to complete. → The color of the fluorescent sewing lines are now being changed for respective seam color, indicating that the sewing is being completed.
content_description: This web page provides a step-by-step guide for creating, folding, and sewing various types of pleats in the 2D Pattern feature of your design software.

title: Can I change my subscription plan?
content: **Question** Can I change my subscription plan? **Answer** You can change the plan at least 24 hours before the next bill due to your current plan. To change the subscription plan from monthly to yearly (or vice versa), 1. Sign in to the CLO web and go to the [Subscription page](https://www.clo3d.com/en/accounts/subscription). 2. Click the "Change Plan" button. 3. Check the current subscription and plan type that will be changed. 4. Click the "Change" button. *Once you change your subscription plan, you can only change the plan again ONLY AFTER you complete purchasing the product on the starting date of the changed plans. Until then, you cannot cancel the changes. Only canceling a subscription is available. *If you change the plan, you will be charged the amount for the changed plan from the next payment date of the existing plan. *If you cancel the subscription, you cannot change the plan type. *Individual plans cannot be changed as student plans and vice versa. To change your license from CLO for Individuals to CLO for Business, please reach out to CLO via [Contact Us](https://www.clo3d.com/support/contactus).
content_description: Learn how to change your subscription plan with CLO, including important guidelines and steps to ensure a smooth transition.

title: Cache Animation Export
content: **Objective** Export Animation cache data. **※ Note:** You can export only the cache data of garments. ** Location** Main Menu ▶ File ▶ Export ▶ Animation * **Maya Cache (.mc) ** * **Maya Cache (.mcx) ** * **Point Cache 2 ** * **MDD Cache (Standard) ** * **MDD Cache (Maya/3ds Max)** ** Operation** 1. Click the tool/menu indicated. → The Save File window appears. 2. Select the desired file and click **OK**. → The Export window opens. 3. Set the full details and click **OK**. **** **Object** | **Unweld/Weld Object** Export the selected objects as unweld or weld objects. **※ Note: **This option is removed from 6.2 and above. ---|--- **Unweld** Exports the Vertex (points of the mesh) of the parts of the pattern that are sewn together into one line into multiple objects. ※ Thickness exports for quad meshes available beginning version. | **Weld** Combines the Vertex (points of the mesh) of the parts of the pattern that are sewn together into one line into one point. **Selected Pattern:** Weld based on the sewing line that connects the selected patterns. **Thin** Ensures that the thickness will not be exported even if the rendering thickness value is increased beforehand. | **Thick** Exports a pattern with its rendering thickness values in its increased state. **Combined UV Coordinates:** Exports all Garment Pattern texture data fit UV Coordinates ranging from 0 to 1. **※Note:** Unified Texture export multiple layers of texture information as a single UV texture information. **Scale** | Adjusts the scale of the file being exported when a value is entered or the desired unit from **Unit in file to import** is selected. **Axis Conversion** | Changes the directions of each axis of the object. **Animation** | Entire Area (saves all of the recorded garment animation.) | Play Area Only (saves only the play area garment animation.) **File** | **Save With Texture Files (.zip):** Exports the .obj file, .mtl file, and texture images used in the garment as one compressed file when exporting animation. **Save with Meta Data (.xml) :** Export the garment's pattern (Mesh), physical property, and sewing information as Meta Data (ver2.3.0). **Diffuse Color Combined on Texture:** Combine and save the garment's texture image and color as a single image (ver2.2.0). **Exclude Ambient Color (for Modo):** Exclude the Ambient color value when saving materials (ver2.2.0).
content_description: This web page provides a comprehensive guide for exporting animation cache data of garments in various formats, including detailed steps for adjusting export settings and options.

title: Apply Graphic Image
content: ### Objective Place graphic images on Patterns. Use this function to express Garment details such as placed prints, embroideries, or logos. **Location** Main Menu ▶ Materials ▶ Graphics ▶ **Graphic (2D Pattern)** /**Graphic (3D Pattern)** 3D or 2D Toolbar ▶ ![Graphic.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115024687648/Graphic.png) **Graphic (2D Pattern)** /**Graphic (3D Pattern)** **Operation** 1. Select the tool/ menu indicate in Location: **→** The file browser appears 2. Click a graphic image and a pattern where the graphic image should be placed. → The Add Graphic window appears. 3. Enter the desired values for the graphic dimensions and position and click OK **Width** | Set the width of the graphic image. ---|--- **Height** | Set the height of the graphic image. ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/article_attachments/115005593967/img_ratio_1.png) | Link or unlink the aspect ratio of the graphic image. **Position** | **Outline** | Set the distance from the left, right, top, or bottom of the graphic outline to the pattern outline. This menu only appears when placing the graphic in the 2D window (ver2.5.0). **Center** | Set the distance from the center of the graphic to the left, right, top, or bottom of the pattern outline. This menu only appears when placing the graphic in the 2D window (ver2.5.0). → Graphic is applied to the pattern. → Graphic is applied to the seam across the pattern pieces as well. (ver 6.0) **※ Note:** * Recommend you to apply and edit the graphic in the 3d window, when you apply the graphic over the seam. * **Add as Graphic** by right-clicking on the image file in the library. * If the AI/PDF file has more than one artboard and layer, select the desired artboard and layer in the preview window. (ver 6.1)
content_description: This web page provides a step-by-step guide for placing graphic images on garment patterns, allowing users to enhance their designs with prints, embroideries, and logos.

title: Snap to Grid
content: **List of Contents** Snap to Grid Set Grid Size **Objective** Draft or modify Patterns and Internal Shapes using grids. ** Location** **Snap to Grid** Main Menu ▶ Preferences ▶ **Snap to Grid** (ver3.2 or earlier) Right Click Pop-Up Menu (on 2D Window) ▶ **Snap to Grid** (ver3.2 or ealier) Main Menu ▶ Preferences ▶ Grid Properties (F12) ▶ 2D Grid ▶ **Snap to Grid** (ver4.0 or later) Right Click Pop-Up Menu (on 3D/2D Window) ▶ Grid Properties (F12) ▶ 2D Grid ▶ **Snap to Grid** (ver4.0 or later) **Set Grid Size** Main Menu ▶ Preferences ▶ **2D Pattern Window Properties/ Grid Properties**(ver3.2 or earlier) Right Click Pop-Up Menu (on 2D Window) ▶ **2D Pattern Window Properties/ Grid Properties**(ver3.2 or earlier) Main Menu ▶ Preferences ▶ Grid Properties (F12) ▶ 2D Grid ▶ **Distance** (ver4.0 or later) Right Click Pop-Up Menu (on 3D/2D Window) ▶ Grid Properties (F12) ▶ 2D Grid ▶ **Distance** (ver4.0 or later) ** Operation** **Snap to Grid** 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ Preferences ▶ **Snap to Grid** Right Click Pop-Up Menu (on 2D Window) ▶ **Snap to Grid** → Patterns and Internal Shapes snap to the grids when moved. **Set Grid Size** 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ Preferences ▶ **2D Pattern Window Properties/ Grid Properties**(ver4.0.0) Right Click Pop-Up Menu (on 2D Window) ▶ **2D Pattern Window Properties/ Grid Properties**(ver4.0.0) 2. Find the **Distance** option in the Property Editor. 3. Enter the desired value. →The grid reflects the change. Go back to the List of Contents
content_description: Discover how to efficiently draft and modify patterns and internal shapes using grid functionalities, including "Snap to Grid" and "Set Grid Size," for enhanced precision in your designs.

title: Select All With Same Property
content: **List of Contents** Select All with Same Property Select All with Same Property from Pop-Up Menu Select All with Same Property from Property Editor **Select All with Same Property** \- Select all Patterns will the same property. \- Right-click on the Pattern and select **Select All with Same Property** from the pop-up menu, or select the same option in the property editor. ** Selected All with Same Property from Pop-Up Menu** ** ** * **Particle Distance** \- Select the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115022656308/mceclip0.png) **Transform Pattern** tool from the 2D toolbar and right click on the desired Pattern. Hover the mouse over **Select All with Same Property** and select **Particle Distance** from the pop-up menu. \- All Patterns with the same particle distance will be selected. * **Layer ** \- Select the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115022656308/mceclip0.png) **Transform Pattern** tool from the 2D toolbar and right click on the desired Pattern. Hover the mouse over **Select All with Same Property** and select **Layer** from the pop-up menu. \- All Patterns with the same layer will be selected. * **Fabric** \- Select the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115022656308/mceclip0.png) **Transform Pattern** tool from the 2D toolbar and right click on the desired Pattern. Hover the mouse over **Select All with Same Property** and select **Fabric** from the pop-up menu. \- All Patterns with the same fabric will be selected. **Select All with Same Property from Property Editor** \- Select the Pattern from the 2D window. \- Navigate to the Property Editor and find **Simulation Properties.** Right-click on the options below the Simulation Properties. Click **Select All with Same Property** to select all patterns with the same respective setting. Go back to the List of Contents
content_description: This web page provides a comprehensive guide on how to efficiently select all patterns with the same properties in the Clo3D design software, utilizing both the pop-up menu and the property editor.

title: Create Smooth Curve
content: **List of Contents** Smooth Curve Smooth Curve Smooth Curve with Specific Value Smooth Curve with Reference Line **Smooth Curve** \- Round corners of Patterns or Internal Shapes. \- Select the ![Toolbar_2D_Curve_RoundCorner.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360002351068/Toolbar_2D_Curve_RoundCorner.png)**Smooth Curve** tool from the 2D toolbar. \- Main Menu > 2D Pattern > Edit > ![Toolbar_2D_Curve_RoundCorner.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360002351068/Toolbar_2D_Curve_RoundCorner.png)**Smooth Curve** **Smooth Curve** \- Hover the mouse over the corner which you wish to curve. \- Click and drag the corner to convert it to a rounded corner. **Smooth Curve with Specific Value** \- To assign a specific length to the rounded corner, right click on the 2D window while click and dragging the desired corner. \- The Round Corner by Length window appears. \- Type in the line length or adjust the curvature. \- Click OK to complete the rounded corner. **Smooth Curve with Reference Line** \- Click Pattern Outlines that make a corner which needs to be rounded. \- A reference line is created between the selected Pattern Outlines. \- Select the side that needs to be rounded. \- Click and drag the reference line to create the desired curve line. Once you release the mouse, the selected side of the Pattern Outline is replaced with the reference line. Go back to the List of Contents
content_description: This web page provides a comprehensive guide on how to use the Smooth Curve tool in Clo3D to round corners of patterns and internal shapes with various methods and specific adjustments.

title: Edit Texture (2D)
content: **List of Contents** Edit Texture (2D) Translate Scale Rotate Rotate Grainline **Edit Texture (2D)** \- Edit texture’s grainline and position per Pattern or scale and rotate texture per fabric. \- Select the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115022191168/mceclip0.png) **Edit Texture (2D)** tool from the 2D Toolbar \- Or, navigate to Main Menu ▶ Materials ▶ Texture ▶ **Edit Texture (2D).** ** ****Translate** \- Select the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115022191168/mceclip0.png)**Edit Texture (2D)** tool from the 2D toolbar. \- Click and drag the texture applied to the Pattern. \- Only the texture within the selected Pattern will be moved. **Scale** * **Scale per Pattern** \- Select the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115022191168/mceclip0.png) **Edit Texture (2D)** tool from the 2D toolbar. \- Select the Pattern that its texture to be scaled as the **Gizmo** is activated on the right top corner of the 2D window. \- Click and drag the diagonal arrow. \- The texture will be scaled, maintaining its height and width ratio. \- Click and drag the vertical or horizontal arrow to vertically or horizontally scale the texture respectively. * **Scale per Fabric ** \- Select the fabric item to be edited in the Object Browser. \- Navigate and type in desired values to Property Editor ▶ Texture Transformation ▶ **Width** or**Height**** **\- Toggle on**Lock Aspect Ratio** to maintain the height and width ratio while scaling the texture. ** ** **Rotate** **** \- Select the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115022191168/mceclip0.png) **Edit Texture (2D)** tool from the 2D toolbar. \- Click on the Pattern that its texture to be edited. \- When the **Gizmo** tool is activated on the right top corner of the 2D window, Click and drag the curved line of the **Gizmo** tool. **Rotate Grainline** * **On Pattern ** \- Select the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115022191168/mceclip0.png) **Edit Texture (2D)** tool from the 2D toolbar. \- Click on the Pattern that its Grainline to be rotated. \- The selected Pattern’s Grainline will be activated as it appears in black. \- Click and drag to rotate the Grainline. \- The selected Pattern’s Grainline and its texture will be rotated towards the direction the mouse was moved. * **In Property Editor ** \- Select the Pattern that its Grainline to be rotated. \- Navigate and type in desired values to Property Editor ▶ Fabric ▶ **Grainline Direction** \- Once Simulation is activated, the drape will change accordingly. Go back to the List of Contents
content_description: This web page provides a comprehensive guide on how to edit 2D textures in CLO3D, including instructions for translating, scaling, rotating, and adjusting grainlines for patterns and fabrics.

title: [Tool] Seamline Topstitch
content: ### Objective Create a Seamline Topstitch. **Location** Main Menu ▶ Materials ▶ Topstitch ▶ **Seamline Topstitch** 2D Toolbar ▶ ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/article_attachments/115005670348/__________.png) **Seamline Topstitch** ** Operation** 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ Materials ▶ Topstitch ▶ **Seamline Topstitch** 2D Toolbar ▶ ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/article_attachments/115005670348/__________.png) **Seamline Topstitch** → All sewing lines on the Pattern are displayed. 2. Click on a point where a Topstitch begins. 3. Move mouse to the direction where the Topstitch is going to be created. 4. Click on another point where the Topstitch ends. → The Topstitch is now being created with being highlighted. **※ Note:** * Click and drag in the 2D window to encompass all segments where Topstitches to be applied. Topstitches appear on all selected segments (ver3.2.0). * Use [lasso selection](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/115004324447) to select Pattern Outlines and Internal Lines where Topstitches should be created on (ver3.2.0). * OBJ Topstitches temporarily disappear when the Simulation is activated, but they appear again when the Simulation is deactivated (ver3.2.0). * Right click when creating the Topstitch to enter specific length (ver4.2.0).
content_description: This webpage provides a step-by-step guide for creating a Seamline Topstitch in your design software, ensuring accurate application and customization of stitching lines on patterns.

title: [Style Property] Topstitch Offset (Inch)
content: ### **Objective** Adjust the interval between Topstitches on Internal Lines or Pattern outlines. ** Location** Object Browser ▶ Topstitch ▶ Topstitch Property Editor ▶ **Offset** ** Operation** 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Object Browser ▶ Topstitch ▶ Topstitch Property Editor ▶ **Offset** 2. Adjust the interval. → The value is now being adjusted and applied. **※ Note :** Offset value appears in inch(in) and this unit of length can be set in millimeter(mm) or centimeter(cm) in the User Setting. When alteration is made in inch(in), it automatically appears in millimeter(mm) or centimeter(cm) and vice versa. ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/article_attachments/115005620527/____95.png)
content_description: This webpage provides guidance on adjusting the interval between topstitches on internal lines or pattern outlines within the Topstitch Property Editor.

title: Auto Sewing (ver 6.0)
content: **Objective** Patterns are automatically sewn based on their placement on avatars. **※Note:** The available range of automatic sewing is as follows, * Garment: * Top (T-shirts, jackets, Jumper, etc.) and One-piece are possible. * Bottom (Skirt, Pants, etc) and Pants are impossible. * Parts: Bodies, Sleeves, Collars, Darts, Pleats, Cuffs, Sleeves with Vend & Placket. * Layers: One-ply patterns such as Pockets and Lining except for two-layer Patterns. **Location** Main Menu ▶ Sewing ▶ **Auto Sewing** 3D Toolbar ▶ **Auto Sewing** **Operation** 1. Click the [Arrangement Points ](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/115001999287-Arrange-Pattern-with-Arrangement-Points-Flip-Wrap-Direction)of the Avatar to arrange the Pattern. Since Auto Sewing is calculated by the information of the Arrangement Points (where each Pattern Piece is arranged), correct Arrangement Points should be used based on the rules below, Otherwise, Auto Sewing may not work properly. (It is only applicable to the Bounding Volumes provided by CLO) **Collar/ Band** | Use Arrangement Points at the Avatar's neck. ---|--- **Bodies** | Use Arrangement Points at the Avatar's body. **Sleeves** | Use Arrangement Points at the Avatar's arm, the cuffs can be used either arm/wrist Arrangement Points. **Bottom (ver 6.1)** | Use Arrangement Points at the legs. **※Note:** Be mindful to arrange the pieces to auto sew correctly. \- If the belt length includes a placket which is placed over the zipper, arrange the placket piece. \- Trace the internal line of the side pocket along side seams. \- If the pants width is large, arrange front and back pattern pieces separately by using each of the arrangement points. 2. Select the tool/menu indicated in Location. → The arranged patterns are automatically sewn. **※Note:** * If sewing has been applied prior to automatic sewing, it is maintained while the rest of the sewing lines are being additionally auto-sewn. * Darts and Pleats can be sewn automatically without arranging patterns. * For Pleats, automatic sewing is possible only when Internal Lines are defined by the fold direction of the Pleats.
content_description: This webpage provides guidelines for automatically sewing patterns on avatars based on their arrangement, ensuring optimal placement and functionality for garment design.

title: Layer Clone (Over)
content: **Layer Clone (Over)** \- Duplicate a Pattern in its draped state and place it directly over the original Pattern. Sewing Lines will be automatically applied to the Pattern outlines and Internal Lines to connect the cloned Pattern to the original Pattern. \- The Layer Clone (Under) function is efficient when creating a double-layered Garment such as padding, collar, cuffs, and more. \- Select the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115021447968/mceclip0.png) **Transform pattern** tool or ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115021447988/mceclip1.png) **Edit Pattern** tool from the 2D toolbar. \- Navigate to the 2D window and right click on the Pattern to be cloned and select **Layer Clone (Over)** from the pop-up menu. \- The cloned Pattern will follow along the mouse. Click on the 2D window to place the cloned Pattern. \- In the 3D window, the cloned Pattern will be directly placed over the original Pattern and its Pattern outlines and Internal Lines will be sewn to the original Pattern. \- The cloned Patterns will be highlighted in light green in the 2D window and the linked editing will be applied.
content_description: The Layer Clone function allows you to efficiently duplicate a pattern in its draped state, enabling the seamless creation of double-layered garments with automatic sewing lines and linked editing features.

title: Strengthen/Unstrengthen
content: **Objective** The Pattern Strengthen is a feature that temporarily applies hard properties to the garment. When a pattern is folded, it can be folded more reliably by receiving a strong force from the line segment applied with the folding angle and if a garment is simulated by overlapping each other, it can be solved by simulating flat with the rigid force of the physical properties. **Location** 3D Toolbar ▶ ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/article_attachments/115005490267/Toolbar_3D_Select_Move.png) **Select/Move** 2D Toolbar ▶ ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/article_attachments/115005490287/Toolbar_2D_Pattern_Transform.png) **Transform Pattern** **Operation** 1. Select the tool/menu indicated in Location. 2. Right-click on the 3D or 2D pattern and click the **Strengthen/Unstrengthen**. → The pattern will be strengthened/unstrengthened. **※Note:** Right-click on the background of the 3D window and hover **Show/Hide Color** **▶** Click the Show **Strengthen** Menu to show or hide the color applied during strengthening. (ver 6.1)
content_description: Learn how to effectively use the Pattern Strengthen feature to enhance garment simulation by applying temporary hard properties for improved folding and overlapping performance.

title: Synchronize Pattern
content: **Objective** **ver2.3.0** All adjustments made in the 2D window **automatically** synchronizes with the 3D window. Simulation automatically ends when making a modification on 2D Pattern while simulating. **ver2.2.0** Once the sync button is activating, any adjustments, not only design adjustments, but also sewing lines, print textures, particle distances get reflected in the 3D window. Even if the synchronization is off, activating the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/article_attachments/115005481127/Toolbar_3D_Simulation.png) **Simulation** tool auto-activates the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/article_attachments/115005529108/___.png) **Sync** tool and reflects on the 3D window. **Location** Main Menu ▶ **Sync** (Ctrl + D) 2D Toolbar ▶ ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/article_attachments/115005529108/___.png) **Sync** (Ctrl + D) ### **Operation** 1\. Make adjustments in the 2D window. 2\. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ **Sync** (Ctrl + D) 2D Toolbar ▶ ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/article_attachments/115005529108/___.png) **Sync** (Ctrl + D) **※ Note:****** **Changes in a Pattern Color According to Synchronization** A Pattern that has never been synchronized appears in transparent. A Pattern that has been synchronized at least once appears in red color, and a Pattern that its synchronization is currently activating appears in blue color.
content_description: This web page provides a guide on how to effectively synchronize adjustments between the 2D and 3D windows in CLO 3D, ensuring real-time updates and efficient simulation management.

title: Can I use Patterns constructed in CLO in the manufacturing process?
content: **Question** Can I use Patterns constructed in CLO in the manufacturing process? **Answer** With slight modification, Patterns created in CLO can be used in the manufacturing process.
content_description: This webpage aims to clarify how Patterns created in CLO can be adapted for use in the manufacturing process.

title: Cut and Cut & Sew
content: **Objective** Divide a Pattern into desired pieces using Internal Lines. ** Location** 3D Toolbar ▶![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/article_attachments/115005644108/Toolbar_3D_Cut_Line_Edit.png)**Edit 3D Pen (Garment)** ** Operation** 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: 3D Toolbar ▶![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/article_attachments/115005644108/Toolbar_3D_Cut_Line_Edit.png) **Edit 3D Pen (Garment)** 2. Click on created Baselines or Internal Lines on 3D Garment. → The selected Baselines or Internal Lines are now being highlighted in yellow color. 3. Right-click on the selected Baselines or Internal Lines. → A Pop-up menu appears. 4. Select **Cut** or **Cut & Sew** in the pop-up menu. → The selected Baselines or Internal Lines are now being cut or cut & sewn.
content_description: This web page provides a step-by-step guide on how to divide a pattern into desired pieces using Internal Lines within the 3D Toolbar in garment design.
